Carolina Casualty  is a member company of  W. R. Berkley Corporation , an insurance holding company that is among the largest commercial lines insurance writers in the United States. We specialize in liability, physical damage, cargo and other insurance solutions for the commercial auto markets including trucking, public transportation and others.

Join Carolina Casualty, where innovation meets purpose.

Carolina Casualty is a proud member of W. R. Berkley Corporation, one of the largest commercial lines insurers in the country. What sets us apart is not just our size, but how we work and who we are.

We specialize in liability, physical damage, cargo, and other insurance solutions for the commercial auto market, including trucking and public transportation industries that keep America moving. Our team tackles real, complex challenges for the people and businesses that make that possible every day.

At CCIC, we live by three simple truths:

Always do right. Integrity is not just a slogan. It guides every decision we make.

Everything counts; everyone matters. Every role, every voice, and every contribution help shape who we are as an organization.

Embrace innovation and act responsibly. We are willing to challenge the status quo while remaining thoughtful and committed to our people, customers, and partners.

If you are looking for a place where your work makes an impact, your ideas are valued, and doing the right thing is expected, we would love to meet you.

The company is an equal opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

We are seeking a Finance Director to support financial planning and analysis (FP&A) within our Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance business. This role combines core finance responsibilities—forecasting, budgeting, and general ledger oversight—with advanced data and analytics capabilities to drive actionable insights and improve financial decision-making. The ideal candidate will act as a bridge between Finance, Actuarial, and Data teams to ensure alignment across financial results, operational drivers, and analytical outputs.

Key Functions/Duties of Position:

Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)
•    Lead the annual budgeting process and periodic forecasting cycles (monthly/quarterly) for P&C lines of business
•    Develop driver-based financial models incorporating premiums, claims, loss ratios, and expenses
•    Analyze variances between actuals, forecasts, and plan; clearly communicate drivers and risks
•    Partner with business leaders to provide financial insights that support strategic planning
General Ledger & Financial Close Support
•    Support close processes by reconciling financial results with underlying operational and actuarial data
•    Perform general ledger “tie-outs” and ensure accuracy of financial reporting
•    Investigate discrepancies across systems (policy admin, claims, finance) and resolve issues
•    Collaborate with Accounting to ensure proper treatment of insurance-specific transactions (e.g., reserves, premium recognition)
Data & Analytics Integration
•    Act as a key liaison between Finance and Data/Analytics teams
•    Translate business and finance requirements into data models, dashboards, and reporting solutions
•    Utilize data tools (e.g., Power BI, SQL, Excel, Python) to automate reporting and generate insights
•    Enhance data governance and ensure consistency across financial and operational metrics
Business Partnering
•    Work closely with Actuarial, Underwriting, and Claims teams to understand business drivers
•    Provide insights on profitability, loss trends, and expense management
•    Support decision-making on pricing, product performance, and cost optimization

Qualifications

Education Requirement
•    Bachelor’s degree in Finance or Accounting

Qualifications:
•    10+ years of experience in FP&A, finance, or accounting
•    Strong understanding of insurance concepts (loss ratios, reserves, premiums, underwriting results), with PNC experience preferred
•    Proven experience in forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis
•    Solid understanding of general ledger structures and financial reporting
Preferred
•    Experience working with actuarial or insurance data sets
•    Advanced Excel skills; familiarity with data tools (Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Python)
•    Advanced degree (MBA or Master’s) in Finance, Accounting, or Business strongly preferred
•    CPA, CFA, preferred or in progress toward certification

Working Conditions and Physical Requirements
Normal office conditions

Additional Company Details

We do not accept any unsolicited resumes from external recruiting agencies or firms.

The company offers a competitive compensation plan and robust benefits package for full time regular employees which for this role include:

• Base Salary Range: $110,000 - $170,000
• Eligible to participate in annual discretionary bonus.
• Benefits: Health, Dental, Vision, Life, Disability, Wellness, Paid Time Off, 401(k) and Profit-Sharing plans.

Offering guaranteed cost options to employers nationwide, Key Risk focuses on delivering products and services within specialized verticals to reduce workers' compensation exposures and deliver industry-leading results.

All products and services are distributed through appointed insurance agents and brokers. Key Risk is a member company of W. R. Berkley Corporation, whose insurance company subsidiaries are rated A+ (Superior), Financial Size Category XV by A.M. Best Company and A+ (Strong), by S&P.

For further information about Key Risk please visit  www.KeyRisk.com

Responsibilities

The PEO Risk Management Specialist provides occupational risk assessment, safety consulting, and risk management services in support of Key Risk's Professional Employer Organization (PEO) program. This role partners closely with PEO clients, brokers, underwriting, claims, and service teams to identify, evaluate, and mitigate workplace risks while supporting client retention, profitability, and growth.
The Specialist serves as a trusted advisor to PEO clients and works collaboratively to implement effective safety and workers' compensation management strategies. Through data analysis, client consultation, training, and proactive service planning, this individual helps improve workplace safety performance, reduce claim frequency and severity, and support sustainable underwriting results.

Key functions include but are not limited to the following:

- Conduct occupational risk assessments and evaluate workplace exposures across diverse industries and client operations.
- Identify safety, regulatory, and workers' compensation risk factors impacting PEO clients.
- Develop and implement safety improvement plans designed to reduce injuries and improve client performance.
- Assist clients in establishing effective safety committees, policies, procedures, and employee training programs.
- Monitor client progress toward safety and risk management objectives and recommend corrective actions when necessary.
- Support development and implementation of return-to-work and transitional duty programs.

o PEO Underwriting Support
- Partner with underwriting during prospect evaluation, onboarding, renewal, and retention activities.
- Evaluate prospective clients and provide risk management recommendations that support underwriting decisions.
- Participate in pre-bind and renewal discussions to identify opportunities and concerns related to workplace risk.
- Assist in evaluating loss trends, claim drivers, and operational changes that may affect account performance.
